method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 11 October, averaging 29.7 on Google's 0-100 scale, 7.6 times the next party (Labor). That is 72% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation rose the most on the previous week, up 8.6 points (+41%); the Greens fell furthest, down 3.9 points (-51%).

Searches for the Greens jumped to 19 on 30 September, 8.3 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “New Australian Greens leader David Shoebridge vows to ‘replace’ Labor” (Politico).
Fastest-rising searches alongside One Nation: “one nation candidates”, “one nation victoria”, “one nation leader”.
victoria: 46 days until Victorians vote on Saturday 28 November 2026.

Across the latest poll from each of 4 pollsters, the Coalition averages 29.2% of the primary vote, Labor 24.5%, One Nation 22.2% and the Greens 14.8%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 53.7 to 46.3 (3 polls), an 8.7-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (50 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (Resolve, 6–10 Oct 2026): Wilson 29%, Carroll 22%, Pickering 14%.
